about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Korean Spinach Namul
recipes.summary: Blanched spinach seasoned with garlic, sesame oil and soy, the quickest banchan on the table.
steps: Blanch the spinach in a large pot of boiling water for 30 seconds until just wilted, then plunge into cold water.
Squeeze out as much water as you can and loosen the clumps with your fingers.
Toss with the garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, spring onion and sesame seeds until evenly coated.
notes: Squeezing well stops the dish becoming watery.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Korean Soybean Sprout Namul
recipes.summary: Crunchy sprouts dressed with sesame oil and garlic, served at room temperature.
steps: Rinse the sprouts and put them in a saucepan with the water and salt.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes until tender but still crunchy, then drain well.
Toss with the garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, spring onion and sesame seeds.
notes: Keep the lid on while cooking to remove the raw bean smell.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Korean Gochugaru Cucumber Ribbons with Sesame and Rice Vinegar
recipes.summary: Cool, crunchy cucumber in a spicy-sweet dressing, a refreshing partner to barbecued meat.
steps: Shave the cucumbers into ribbons with a vegetable peeler and toss with the salt.
Leave for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess liquid.
Toss with the vinegar, sugar, chilli, garlic, sesame oil and seeds until coated.
notes: Serve within an hour for the best crunch.
Reduce the chilli for a milder side.

recipes.title: Korean Zucchini Stir-Fry Hobak Bokkeum
recipes.summary: Soft golden zucchini half-moons with garlic and sesame, gently salted.
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and add the zucchini and salt.
Stir-fry for 5 minutes until golden at the edges and tender.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then finish with the sesame oil, spring onion and seeds.
notes: Do not crowd the pan or the zucchini will steam.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Korean Radish Salad Musaengchae
recipes.summary: A crunchy, tangy radish salad in a chilli-vinegar dressing, perfect with fatty meat.

items: 400g daikon radish, cut into fine matchsticks

steps: Toss the radish with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze lightly.
Mix the chilli flakes, vinegar, sugar, garlic and fish sauce into a dressing.
Toss the radish with the dressing, spring onion and sesame seeds until well coated.
notes: Best eaten within 2 days.
Add a little more sugar if the radish is sharp.

recipes.title: Korean Mushroom Bokkeum
recipes.summary: Browned mixed mushrooms with garlic and soy, a savoury side that takes 10 minutes.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over high heat and cook the mushrooms in a single layer for 6 minutes without stirring too often, until well browned.
Add the garlic, soy sauce and sugar and cook for 1 minute until sticky.
Finish with the sesame oil, spring onion and seeds.
notes: Cook in two batches if your pan is small.
Keeps for 3 days.

recipes.title: Korean Carrot Stir-Fry Namul
recipes.summary: Thin carrot strips tossed with garlic and sesame, a sweet and colourful plate filler.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and add the carrots with the salt.
Stir-fry for 5 minutes until just tender but still bright.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then turn off the heat and finish with the sesame oil and seeds.
notes: Serve warm or cold.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Korean Eggplant Namul Gaji Muchim
recipes.summary: Steamed eggplant strips pulled apart and dressed in a garlicky soy and sesame sauce.
steps: Steam the eggplant halves for 12 minutes until completely soft, then cool for 5 minutes.
Tear into long strips and gently squeeze out excess moisture.
Toss with the garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, spring onion and seeds.
notes: Use a pot with a steamer basket or a bamboo steamer.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Korean Fresh Cabbage Kimchi Geotjeori
recipes.summary: Unfermented fresh kimchi with a chilli, garlic and fish sauce dressing, ready to eat straight away.
steps: Cut the cabbage into bite-sized pieces and toss with the salt, then leave for 15 minutes and squeeze out the liquid.
Mix the chilli flakes, garlic, fish sauce, sugar and ginger into a paste.
Toss the cabbage with the paste, spring onions and sesame seeds until every piece is coated.
notes: Eat within 3 days; it is a fresh salad, not a fermented kimchi.
Wear gloves when mixing the chilli paste.

recipes.title: Gyeran Mari Layered Korean Egg Roll with Carrot and Spring Onion
recipes.summary: A tender rolled omelette studded with finely chopped vegetables, sliced into rounds.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the salt and soy sauce, then stir in the carrot and spring onions.
Heat a little oil in a small non-stick frying pan over low heat and pour in a thin layer of egg, cooking until the surface is just set.
Roll the omelette to one end, add more egg to the empty space, cook until set, and roll again, repeating until all the egg is used.
Slide onto a board, rest for 2 minutes and slice into rounds.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm throughout, with no runny egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Use low heat so the outside does not brown.

recipes.title: Japanese Spinach Ohitashi
recipes.summary: Blanched spinach steeped in a light soy and mirin sauce, served chilled.
steps: Heat the soy sauce, mirin, water and sugar in a small saucepan until just simmering, then cool completely.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 40 seconds until just tender, cool in iced water and squeeze dry.
Cut into 4cm lengths, arrange in a bowl, pour over the cooled sauce and scatter with sesame seeds.
notes: The spinach will keep absorbing flavour for a day.
Serve cold in small bowls.

recipes.title: Japanese Green Bean Goma-ae
recipes.summary: Crisp green beans tossed in a nutty, sweet sesame dressing.
steps: Boil the beans in salted water for 3 minutes until bright green and just tender, then drain and refresh in cold water.
Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar or spice grinder until mostly crushed.
Mix with the soy sauce, sugar and mirin, then toss with the beans until coated.
notes: Do not grind the sesame to a paste, a little texture is lovely.
Serve cold or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Japanese Carrot Kinpira
recipes.summary: Sweet and savoury sautéed carrot and capsicum matchsticks with sesame.
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the carrot for 4 minutes until it begins to soften.
Add the capsicum and cook for 2 minutes more.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and chilli and toss until the liquid is nearly gone and the vegetables glossy, then top with sesame seeds.
notes: Serve warm or cold in a bento.
Keeps for 4 days.

recipes.title: Sunomono Thin Cucumber Slices in Sweet Rice Vinegar Dressing
recipes.summary: Salted cucumber in a light sweet vinegar dressing, served cold between rich dishes.
steps: Toss the cucumber with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and soy sauce together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber with the dressing and ginger, then pile into small bowls with sesame seeds on top.
notes: Serve chilled.
Best eaten within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Shiozuke Salted Cabbage with Yuzu-Style Lemon and Chilli
recipes.summary: A crisp, lightly salted cabbage pickle with lemon zest and chilli.
steps: Massage the cabbage with the salt in a bowl for 2 minutes until it begins to release liquid.
Add the lemon zest, juice, chilli and sugar and press down firmly.
Leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid and serve.
notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge in a sealed jar.
Squeezing out the brine keeps it crunchy.

recipes.title: Asazuke Overnight Ginger Cucumber Salted Pickle
recipes.summary: Thick cucumber slices lightly pickled in salt, ginger and brine for a crunchy side.

items: 3 Lebanese cucumbers, cut into thick slices

steps: Put the cucumber, salt, ginger, sugar, vinegar and chilli in a zip-lock bag.
Massage the bag for 1 minute until the cucumber starts to release liquid.
Press out the air, seal and chill until the cucumbers taste lightly pickled, at least 2 hours.
notes: Drain before serving.
Keeps for 2 days.

recipes.title: Creamy Japanese Potato Salad with Cucumber and Carrot Crunch
recipes.summary: A silky, mashed potato salad with Japanese-style mayonnaise, cucumber and ham.

items: 600g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Boil the potatoes and carrot in salted water for 15 to 18 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.
Drain and let the steam escape for 5 minutes, then roughly mash with the vinegar, sugar and salt.
Salt the cucumber slices, squeeze out the liquid and fold into the cooled potato with the mayonnaise, ham and pepper.
notes: Cool the potatoes fully before adding mayonnaise.
Keep chilled and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Hiyayakko Silken Tofu Block with Ginger Soy Topping
recipes.summary: Chilled silken tofu with ginger, spring onion and soy, light and quick.
steps: Drain the tofu gently and keep it chilled until cold, then cut into four blocks.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Place the tofu on plates, top with ginger, spring onion and sesame seeds, and spoon over the sauce.
notes: Keep the tofu chilled until the last minute.
Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Nasu Dengaku Grilled Eggplant Halves under Sweet White Miso Glaze
recipes.summary: Silky grilled eggplant halves under a caramelised sweet miso glaze.
steps: Score the cut side of the eggplants, brush with the oil and roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir the miso, mirin and sugar together and spread on the eggplants.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the glaze is bubbling and caramelised at the edges, then scatter with the sesame seeds.
notes: Watch the glaze closely because miso burns easily.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Japanese Simmered Pumpkin Nimono
recipes.summary: Soft pumpkin chunks simmered in sweet soy until glazed, a gentle home-style side.
steps: Arrange the pumpkin skin-side down in a wide saucepan and add the water, soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the pumpkin is tender when pierced.
Uncover and cook for 3 minutes more until the liquid is reduced to a glaze.
notes: Do not stir, to keep the pieces intact.
Serve warm or cold.

recipes.title: Broccoli Florets in Creamy Toasted Sesame Tahini Dressing Goma-Dare
recipes.summary: Bright green broccoli in a nutty, creamy sesame dressing with a touch of sweetness.
steps: Steam or boil the broccoli for 3 to 4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and water until smooth and pourable.
Arrange the broccoli on a plate, spoon over the dressing and finish with sesame seeds.
notes: Add more water if the dressing is too thick.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Japanese Cabbage Sesame Salad
recipes.summary: A crunchy shredded cabbage salad with a toasted sesame and rice vinegar dressing.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan for 2 minutes until golden, then cool.
Whisk the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar together.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the dressing and sesame seeds just before serving.
notes: Dress it just before eating to keep the crunch.
Keeps shredded cabbage fresh in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.title: Gamja Jorim Glossy Korean Baby Potatoes in Soy and Honey
recipes.summary: Small potatoes simmered in a sweet soy glaze until sticky and glossy.
steps: Fry the potatoes in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes until lightly golden.
Add the soy sauce, honey, sugar and water, then simmer for 18 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potatoes are tender and the sauce reduces to a glaze.
Stir in the sesame oil and sprinkle with the seeds.
notes: Add a small splash of water if the sauce reduces too fast.
Serve warm or cold.
